title: Painting Techniques: Foundations
welcome_lead: Meet the three big paint families — watercolour, acrylic and oil — and what each one is best at.
meta_desc: GCSE painting foundations: watercolour, acrylic, oil paint and their properties.
final_note: Choose paint like a tool — fit it to the job.

concepts.def: Plastic-based paint, dries quickly, very flexible.
Pigment in oil; slow drying, rich blending.
Substance that holds pigment to a surface.
Prepared base layer before painting begins.

walkthroughs.body_html: Watercolour uses gum arabic to bind pigment, thinned with water. It is transparent, so the white of the paper does the lightening — there is no white paint to add. Work light to dark and accept that mistakes are hard to undo.

Acrylic uses a plastic polymer binder. It is water-soluble when wet, waterproof when dry, and dries in minutes. You can use it thin like watercolour or thick like oil. Brushes must be cleaned before paint dries on them.
Oil paint mixes pigment with linseed oil. It can stay wet on the palette for days, allowing soft blending. Always paint fat over lean — more oily layers on top of leaner ones — to avoid cracking.
